# AFD — Agent-First Development

> AFD is a methodology plus TypeScript, Python, Rust and C++ libraries for building software where AI agents are first-class users. Commands are the product: define each capability as a typed command, validate it through the CLI, and only then build UI as a thin surface over it. Humans, scripts and agents (over MCP or in-process) all call the same commands and get the same CommandResult.

Contract: 1.0-rc (the shared specification in `spec/`; each package keeps its own version)
License: MIT
Repository: https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd

The same repository holds the rest of the AFD family: Specimen, FAST-AF, Violet, Umbel, Loam, Botcore and Health. See "The AFD family" below.

## Core ideas

- The honesty check: "If it can't be done via CLI, the architecture is wrong." No UI-only code paths.
- Jobs first: a feature starts from the jobs it serves, each written as a scenario file before its commands are specified.
- Workflow per command: Define (typed schema, named errors) → Validate (call it from the terminal, cover edge cases) → Surface (UI wraps a command that already passes).
- CommandResult: every command returns `success` plus `data` or `error`, and can add trust signals: `confidence` (0–1), `reasoning`, `warnings`, `suggestions`, `sources`, `plan`, `alternatives`.
- Errors carry `code`, `message`, `suggestion` and `retryable`, so an agent can recover instead of stalling.
- Command naming is `domain-action` kebab-case: `todo-create`, `user-get`, `order-list`.
- Testing targets the job, not the UI: YAML JTBD scenarios call commands step by step, and surface validation audits the command set for collisions, schema drift and prompt injection.
- One contract across languages: a 34-case conformance suite runs in CI against TypeScript, Python, Rust and C++ backends.
- AFD is UX design for non-human users. Each classic interface pattern has an agent equivalent that AFD ships as command metadata (see "Agent UX" below).

## Install

- TypeScript: `npm install @lushly-dev/afd-server @lushly-dev/afd-cli zod`
- Python: `pip install afd`
- Rust: `cargo add afd`
- C++: CMake `FetchContent` from `https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd.git` with `SOURCE_SUBDIR packages/cpp`, then link `afd::afd`. Use the published `GIT_TAG cpp-v0.2.0`.

## Minimal command (TypeScript)

```ts
import { defineCommand, success } from '@lushly-dev/afd-server';
import { z } from 'zod';

export const createTodo = defineCommand({
  name: 'todo-create',
  description: 'Create a new todo item',
  expose: { mcp: true },
  input: z.object({ title: z.string().min(1) }),
  async handler(input) {
    const todo = store.create(input);
    return success(todo, { reasoning: `Created "${todo.title}"`, confidence: 1 });
  },
});
```

Serve it with `createMcpServer({ name, version, commands: [createTodo], transport: 'http', port: 3100 }).start()`, then validate it:

```bash
npx afd connect http://localhost:3100/mcp
npx afd call todo-create '{"title":"Buy groceries"}'
```

Full walkthrough: [5-minute quickstart](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd#quickstart)

## Agent UX (human UX pattern → AFD mechanism)

- Progressive disclosure → tool strategies: `toolStrategy: 'grouped'` (default, one tool per category), `'individual'`, or `'lazy'` (five meta-tools: afd-discover, afd-detail, afd-call, afd-batch, afd-pipe). [Guide](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/blob/main/.claude/skills/afd/references/mcp-integration.md)
- Confirmation dialogs → `destructive: true` with `confirmPrompt`. [Guide](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/blob/main/.claude/skills/afd/references/command-trust-config.md)
- Permissions → per-surface `expose: { palette, agent, mcp, cli }`; `mcp` and `cli` are opt-in. [Guide](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/blob/main/.claude/skills/afd/references/command-trust-config.md)
- Undo → `undoable: true`.
- Helpful errors → every error has `code`, `message`, `suggestion`, optional `retryable`. [Guide](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/blob/main/.claude/skills/afd/references/command-schema.md)
- Wayfinding → `requires: ['auth-sign-in']` declares prerequisites, exposed as `_meta.requires`.
- Affordances → `examples` (validated at define time) and `output` schemas.
- Usability testing → `afd validate --surface` lints the command set for collisions, overlap, injection and schema complexity. [Guide](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/blob/main/.claude/skills/afd/references/surface-validation.md)
- Help menu → `bootstrap: true` adds `afd-help`, `afd-docs`, `afd-schema`. [Guide](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/blob/main/.claude/skills/afd/references/mcp-integration.md)

## For coding agents

The repo ships agent skills (SKILL.md format, read by Claude Code, Codex and others): afd, afd-typescript, afd-python, afd-rust, afd-cpp, afd-auth, afd-directclient. Add one to a project with:

```bash
npx degit lushly-dev/afd/.claude/skills/afd .claude/skills/afd
```

Recommended loop: edit a command handler, `afd call` it, read `error.suggestion`, fix, then `afd scenario run scenarios/ --server <url>`.

## Packages

- [@lushly-dev/afd-core](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lushly-dev/afd-core): CommandResult, CommandError, batching, streaming, pipelines
- [@lushly-dev/afd-server](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lushly-dev/afd-server): Zod commands, MCP server factory, middleware, and a browser-safe in-process registry (`/direct`)
- [@lushly-dev/afd-client](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lushly-dev/afd-client): MCP client over Streamable HTTP, and DirectClient (~0.03 ms in-process calls)
- [@lushly-dev/afd-cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lushly-dev/afd-cli): connect, call, validate and explore commands
- [@lushly-dev/afd-testing](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lushly-dev/afd-testing): JTBD scenario runner, surface validation, mock servers
- [@lushly-dev/afd-auth](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lushly-dev/afd-auth): provider-agnostic auth adapter, middleware, session sync
- [@lushly-dev/afd-view-state](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lushly-dev/afd-view-state): UI view state managed through commands
- [@lushly-dev/afd-adapters](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lushly-dev/afd-adapters): render CommandResult as themed HTML
- [@lushly-dev/local-db](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lushly-dev/local-db): async data adapter with swappable backends (memory, HTTP)
- [afd on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/afd/): Python implementation (Pydantic, the MCP SDK): server, client, DirectClient, CLI, testing
- [afd for Rust](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/tree/main/packages/rust): CommandResult types, CommandRegistry, WASM-compatible; an MCP server behind the optional `server` feature
- [afd-cpp](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/tree/main/packages/cpp): C++20 CommandRegistry, DirectClient, batch, pipeline and stream execution; builds without exceptions or RTTI and for WebAssembly

## The AFD family

Projects in the same repository that take the method one layer up. Foundations (Specimen, FAST-AF, Violet) have no dependency on AFD; a separate integration package exposes each one's operations as AFD commands. Status is given per project; "in the repository" means it builds and is tested there but is not published.

- [Specimen](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/tree/main/foundations/specimen): a component observation bench. Renders a component in Chromium and records geometry, computed styles, native control state, open shadow DOM and ARIA snapshots, so two renders can be compared. Runs Storybook-format stories without Storybook. Preview on npm: `npm install @lushly-dev/specimen@preview`, with `@lushly-dev/specimen-cli@preview` (the `specimen` JSON CLI), `@lushly-dev/specimen-afd@preview` (`specimen-*` AFD commands) and `@lushly-dev/specimen-fast-af@preview` (FAST-AF plugin).
- [FAST-AF](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/tree/main/foundations/fast-af): a web component runtime, `@lushly-dev/fast-element` (preview on npm: `npm install @lushly-dev/fast-element@preview`), and a component library built on it, `violet-elements` (in the repository). Every component's stories run on Specimen, and each component has a pack record of what an agent writing a page needs to know.
- [Violet](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/tree/main/foundations/violet): a hierarchical design token engine. Nodes inherit tokens from their parents and add, override or remove them; exports CSS, SCSS, TypeScript, JSON, Swift, Kotlin, Dart, Tailwind and Lua. Includes a browser runtime, a `violet` CLI and a `violet-mcp` server. In the repository.
- [Umbel](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/tree/main/endpoints/umbel): an empty Rust host for capability plugins, over MCP (stdio and Streamable HTTP) and as a CLI. Knowledge, memory and context are first-party plugins; one deployment holds several isolated spaces. In development, unpublished. [Status](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/blob/main/endpoints/umbel/docs/STATUS.md).
- [Loam](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/tree/main/endpoints/loam): an application shell in TypeScript. Apps land as plugins and share sign-in, projects, documents and a command palette; the shell's own state is commands. Its chrome is FAST-AF components on a Violet theme. In development, unpublished. [Status](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/blob/main/endpoints/loam/docs/STATUS.md).
- [Botcore](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/tree/main/endpoints/botcore): shared agent tooling (commands, skills, configuration, plugins) built on AFD. On PyPI as `lushly-botcore`.
- [Health](https://github.com/lushly-dev/afd/tree/main/endpoints/health): repository health audits with a versioned JSON report, and a static dashboard to read it. In the repository.
